newsitem.title: UK: Britain's last Hong Kong serviceman close to tears.
newsitem.headline: Britain's last Hong Kong serviceman close to tears.

text.p: The last British serviceman to leave Hong Kong, Squadron Leader Lee Doherty, arrived back in London on Tuesday and admitted he came close to tears as he stepped from the former colony's soil.

As the man in charge of the military movements unit in Hong Kong, Doherty had the task of getting 500 servicemen onto the last two flights out. He had arranged the movement of hundreds of passengers and tonnes of equipment over the last few months ahead of the handover to China at midnight on Monday.
Doherty arrived at London's Heathrow Airport aboard a chartered British Airways jumbo jet to a joyful reunion with his wife Joanna.
"As I came to go up the stairway (in Hong Kong) I knew that there was nobody behind me, that's it, there's nothing left.
"When I got to the top of the steps there was a sense of relief which generated the emotion. It was a pretty emotional moment," Doherty said.
Asked if he shed any tears, he said: "They may have been welling -- I'll go that far."

Speaking about the British forces' departure from Hong Kong, he added: "It was a sense of achievement but at that stage there was a degree of sadness. We were happy that we were going to make the deadline and were coming back to the UK. We had a sense of a job well done."
Doherty was among 256 British servicemen who arrived at Heathrow on Tuesday on the last British military flight out of Hong Kong.

Among them was Lieutenant-Colonel Jeremy Ellis, the commanding officer of the Queen's Gurkha Signals Regiment and the camp commandant of the Prince of Wales barracks -- the last British military establishment in Hong Kong.
He said that it was 10 seconds to midnight on Monday when he handed over the barracks to the Chinese People's Liberation Army as they marched into Hong Kong.
